🗞 BEAT THE STREET BULLETIN 🗞
Date: 14 August 2026
Telegram: [https://t.me/BeatTheStreetnews]

* 📍 ORDER WIN

KALPATARU PROJECTS: Secures new orders worth ~₹3,526 Cr across industrial EPC, Power T&D and residential buildings, taking FY27 YTD order intake above ₹11,000 Cr.

ENGINEERS INDIA: Secures Q1 orders worth ~₹478 Cr, including a ₹286 Cr PMC & EPCM contract for a fertilizer plant in Ethiopia and ₹134.6 Cr ONGC order.

TRANSFORMERS & RECTIFIERS INDIA: Receives a large transformer order from APTRANSCO valued between ₹100–500 Cr, with execution scheduled within 13 months.

REFEX INDUSTRIES: Bags ₹40.83 Cr ash transportation contract from a major power producer for NHAI and government road projects.

DESCO INFRATECH: Wins purchase/service orders worth ₹2.14 Cr from KP Energy, Adani Total Gas and Maharashtra Natural Gas.

DMR ENGINEERING: Wins ₹1.66 Cr, 8-year Project Management Agency contract from Adani Renewable Energy One for the 1,500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project.

* 📍 ACQUISITION

ADANI ENERGY SOLUTIONS: Acquires 100% stake in Vizag Power Transmission Ltd for ₹5 lakh to facilitate power evacuation for proposed 4,500 MW green hydrogen/ammonia projects in Vizag.

GREAVES COTTON: Acquires the remaining 20% stake in Excel Controlinkage, taking ownership to 100% and making it a wholly-owned subsidiary.

RAINBOW CHILDREN’S MEDICARE: Completes acquisition of 64% partnership interest in Super Prime Medical Care LLP.

* 📍 COLLABORATION

SHUKRA PHARMA: Signs term sheet with Singapore-based Borns Medical Robotics to form a 60:40 JV for AI-enabled surgical robotic systems in India and Asia-Pacific.

PAISALO DIGITAL: Signs MOU with Chakrawiu to provide AI, software development, automation and technology services, with expected annual other income of ~₹4–5 Cr.

* 📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

GLAND PHARMA: Appoints Deepak Sapra as CEO effective November 16, 2026; brings 27 years of executive experience across pharma, APIs, CDMO and global markets.

* 📍 NEW PROJECTS

JUNIPER HOTELS: Plans ~₹850 Cr investment to develop a ~550-key luxury 5-star hotel in Dwarka, New Delhi, targeted for completion by 2030.

PRAKASH PIPES: Plans ₹100 Cr capex to double flexible packaging capacity to 52,800 MTPA at Kashipur by March 2027.

DCW: Approves up to ₹250 Cr investment over 2–3 years to expand Synthetic Iron Oxide Pigments capacity by 50% and improve its Sahupuram power plant.

ADITYA BIRLA REAL ESTATE: Plans ₹9,600 Cr of FY27 launches and targets ₹15,000 Cr annual pre-sales within 2–3 years.

MAX HEALTHCARE: Plans major capacity additions across Lucknow, Gurgaon, Bhubaneswar, Nagpur, Mohali, Pithampura, Nanavati, Dwarka and Vaishali.

FIEM INDUSTRIES: Plans ₹100–110 Cr FY27 capex mainly for South India capacity expansion to support OEM and EV demand.

GOLKUNDA DIAMONDS: Plans to launch a lab-grown diamond jewellery B2C offering around Diwali 2026.

IRCTC: Plans four new Rail Neer facilities, with land allotted at Prayagraj, Mysore and Ranchi, alongside ongoing capacity expansion.

* 📍 FUNDRAISING

ZEE ENTERTAINMENT ENTERPRISES: SAT allows promoter fundraising; shareholders approve ₹3,143.52 Cr preferential issue of 24.95 Cr fully convertible warrants to Sunbright Mauritius at ₹126 per warrant.

* 📍 CREDIT RATINGS

VEDANTA ALUMINIUM: India Ratings upgrades VAML’s long-term rating to IND AA+/Stable from IND AA-/Rating Watch with Developing Implications.

* 📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

AUROBINDO PHARMA: USFDA issues Warning Letter to Eugia Pharma Specialities Unit-I, which contributes ~2% of group revenue; company says existing US supplies are unaffected.

ALKEM LABORATORIES: Daman formulation facility receives OAI status in August 2026, while US sales grew 6.5% YoY and non-US sales surged 34.5% in Q1.

* 📍 TAX ORDER

ACE / SANGHVI MOVERS / CROWN LIFTERS: Goa Cabinet approves annual road-tax option for construction equipment vehicles at 1% of vehicle cost, replacing the earlier one-time-only system.

* 📍 LAUNCHES

MAHINDRA & MAHINDRA: Set to launch Scorpio-N pickup on August 14 and BE 6 Sporteq on August 15, with the latter featuring a triple-screen dashboard.

ASHOK LEYLAND: Launches industry-first Air Suspension Technology for multi-axle trucks to improve payload and total cost of ownership.

* 📍 ADDITIONS

MAN INDUSTRIES: Gets QatarEnergy Preferred Manufacturers List approval for LSAW pipes, coating and bends, opening access to large-diameter pipe opportunities across QatarEnergy projects.

* 📍 OTHERS

AUTOLINE INDUSTRIES: Q1 revenue rises 74.7% YoY to ₹265.47 Cr and EBITDA grows 41.2% to ₹19.17 Cr; FY27 revenue growth target remains ~30–40% CAGR with 10%+ EBITDA margin.

VASCON ENGINEERS: Maintains ₹1,200 Cr FY27 revenue guidance despite weak Q1, with ~70% of revenue expected in H2 and ₹1,500–2,000 Cr EPC order inflows targeted.

PRAKASH PIPES: Q1 net sales rise 19% to ₹241 Cr, EBITDA jumps 47% to ₹27 Cr and PAT surges 59% to ₹16 Cr, supported by strong packaging exports.

INDIGO PAINTS: Shifts focus toward aggressive revenue growth through higher trade and influencer spending, while margins may moderate slightly in Q2.

ASHOK LEYLAND: Reports record Q1 volumes of 48,763 units, revenue of ₹9,634 Cr and PAT of ₹609 Cr; net cash strengthens to ₹2,252 Cr.

ASHOK LEYLAND: Approves up to £25 Mn investment in Optare and ₹500 Cr investment in Hinduja Housing Finance to support EV expansion and CV financing.

NAVA: Reports record quarterly income of ₹1,268.8 Cr, EBITDA of ₹583.5 Cr and PAT of ₹332.8 Cr, with Maamba Solar’s 100 MW project nearing completion.

ANUPAM RASAYAN: Q1 revenue grows 36% YoY and signs 10-year BASQUEVOLT LOI representing potential revenue opportunity of ~US$300 Mn.

MAX HEALTHCARE: Expects ARPOB growth to remain above inflation, supported by price hikes and adoption of newer treatments, while maintaining flexibility for strategic acquisitions.

ALKEM LABORATORIES: Domestic business grows 13.2% YoY, outperforming IPM by 120 bps, while US sales rise 6.5% and non-US sales jump 34.5%.

SRI LOTUS DEVELOPERS: Subsidiary appointed developer for a premium residential redevelopment project at Shivaji Park Beach Front, Mumbai.

VEDANTA: Wins Punnam Manganese Block in Andhra Pradesh through e-auction, strengthening its diversified metals and mining portfolio.

AJC JEWEL MANUFACTURERS: Q1 total income surges 124.69% YoY to ₹101.38 Cr and PAT jumps 318.7% to ₹2.38 Cr; targets ~50% revenue CAGR over three years.

TIL: Standalone order book stands at ₹211 Cr and consolidated TIL-TCPL order book at ₹539 Cr, while Q1 Reach Stacker deliveries hit a record 9 units.

AMBER ENTERPRISES: Maintains ~40% FY27 electronics growth guidance and expects margins to normalize to 15–16% from H2 FY27 as cost pass-through improves.

COAL INDIA / L&T: Among 20 bidders for the government’s ₹7,280 Cr rare-earth permanent magnet manufacturing scheme targeting 6,000 MTPA domestic capacity.

APOLLO HOSPITALS: Targets 20% hospital revenue growth, with HealthCo digital expected to reach breakeven next quarter and diagnostics targeting 20%+ growth.

PROSTARM INFO SYSTEMS: Maintains 25%+ FY27 revenue growth guidance and targets 12–13% EBITDA margin, with bids worth ₹2,000+ Cr under evaluation.

ELDECO HOUSING: Plans ~3.4 million sq ft launches in FY27 and sees FY28 as a pivotal growth year, supported by a newly contracted 50-acre land parcel.

BOSCH: Expects ~8% Q2 growth, with ADAS adoption and upcoming CAFE Phase 3 regulations expected to create significant long-term growth opportunities.

ONE POINT ONE SOLUTIONS: FY27 revenue could potentially double, supported by organic growth, acquisitions and increasing contribution from its Resolux AI platform.

VA TECH WABAG: Targets the higher end of 15–20% medium-term growth guidance and 13–14% FY27 EBITDA margin, with order backlog/revenue expected to remain above 3x.

FOODS & INNS: Targets 20% domestic volume growth in FY27, while frozen foods revenue is targeted to rise from $12 Mn to over $30 Mn over three years.

FIEM INDUSTRIES: Maintains 15–20% FY27 revenue growth guidance and ~14% EBITDA margin, with EV and premiumisation expected to drive two-wheeler growth.

PENNAR INDUSTRIES: Expects double-digit revenue growth from Q2 and reiterates at least 20% FY27 PAT growth, supported by a ₹1,108 Cr India PEB order backlog.

MARKSANS PHARMA: Maintains 15–20% FY27 revenue growth and 20–21% EBITDA margin guidance, while evaluating manufacturing-facility acquisitions.

SHREE PUSHKAR: Targets ₹1,250 Cr FY27 revenue with upside to ₹1,300–1,400 Cr, while Unit 6 is expected to become a major growth driver from FY28.

BATA INDIA: Expects delayed Q1 monsoon revenue to spill into Q2, with premiumisation, franchise expansion and digital channels supporting future growth.

ARMAN FINANCIAL: Targets opex-to-AUM ratio of 7% by FY27-end and credit costs around 2.5–3%, while pursuing lower funding costs and potential rating upgrades.

PAGE INDUSTRIES: Maintains double-digit FY27 volume growth and 19–21% EBITDA margin guidance, with Q1 spillover and price-hike benefits expected from Q2.

FINKURVE FINANCIAL: Reiterates 50–60% FY27 AUM growth guidance and targets increasing co-lending share to 15–20% by FY27-end.

MINDA CORPORATION: Targets 11.5–12% FY27 EBITDA margin and 20–24% growth for Flash Electronics, with ~₹400 Cr FY27 capex planned.

DREAMFOLKS: Targets EBITDA breakeven by FY28 and sees potential for a ₹500 Cr railway-lounge business over the next five years.

RVNL: Targets 15% FY27 revenue growth and 15–20% profit growth, with plans to achieve a 50:50 mix between traditional railway works and competitive projects.

SPENCER’S RETAIL: Expects sales-led EBITDA recovery to continue through FY27, with Jiffy targeting ~25% online growth and Nature’s Basket returning to double-digit growth from Q3.

S.P. APPARELS: Maintains ₹2,000 Cr FY27 revenue target, with H2 growth expected to accelerate on stronger orders and normalized shipments.

WELSPUN LIVING: Targets double-digit FY27 revenue growth and low-teens EBITDA margin, with India-UK FTA expected to improve UK competitiveness.

TEGA INDUSTRIES: Maintains 15% long-term consumables CAGR and expects consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin around 15%, with Tega-Molycop cross-selling to ramp up from Q3/Q4.

PETRONET LNG: Expects Q2 utilisation to improve and plans ~₹9,064 Cr FY27 capex, primarily for its petrochemical project.

MAX FINANCIAL SERVICES: Targets VNB growth ahead of APE growth, focusing on margin expansion and continued distribution expansion.

VST TILLERS: Expects 16–20% power-tiller growth and 50–60% power-weeder growth, while targeting ₹3,000 Cr revenue by 2030.

FIRSTCRY: Expects elevated India growth through FY27 and plans ~100 net new stores, with margin recovery expected as competitive intensity in diapers moderates.

HONASA CONSUMER: Expects FY27 growth to beat long-term high-teens CAGR guidance and EBITDA margin to improve 150–200 bps YoY.

GMR AIRPORTS: Expects stronger H2 passenger traffic recovery, while non-aero businesses target 15–18% annual growth and borrowing costs below 10%.

AXISCADES: Targets ₹1,377 Cr FY27 revenue and ₹270 Cr EBITDA, with four acquisitions planned across Aerospace and Zeda by FY27-end.

AWFIS: Targets ₹1,800+ Cr FY27 revenue and ₹190–200 Cr cash EBITDA, with 22,000–25,000 gross seats planned to be added.

SAMMAAN CAPITAL: Targets ₹30,000 Cr FY27 disbursements and ₹40,000–50,000 Cr in FY28, while evaluating acquisitions from FY28.

INDIA-US TRADE: Trump says the India-US trade deal remains on, while the applicable US tariff on India temporarily falls to 10% following the US Supreme Court’s IEEPA tariff ruling.

NEULAND LABS: USFDA INSPECTION ENDS WITH ONE OBSERVATION

• 🇺🇸 USFDA inspected the company’s Unit 3 manufacturing facility at Gaddapotharam, Telangana from August 10–14, 2026.

• 📋 Inspection concluded with Form 483 containing one observation.

• 🔍 Observation relates to procedural improvements in water and environmental monitoring to include new organisms beyond those listed in USP.

• 📝 Company will submit its response to the USFDA within stipulated timelines.

🟡 Impact: Neutral to Mild Negative — only one observation, but regulatory remediation and USFDA closure remain key monitorables.

reports.text:
Sansera builds precision metal parts for cars, planes, and chip-making machines. Its aerospace and semiconductor order book jumped to Rs 5750 crore from Rs 4464 crore in 3 months, after winning Rs 1250 crore deal from single semiconductor equipment maker. 

That customer builds machines used inside chip factories. Global spending on such machines crossed $143B in 2026 because AI needs more chips than factories can produce. 

Sansera machines complex metal chambers these factories require. Revenue from this deal starts in 2027 and peaks in 2029. >>

Non-auto sales more than doubled. EBITDA margin improved to 19.2% from 17.2%, means company kept more of each rupee earned. 

Aerospace and semiconductor work brought in Rs 315 crore last year and targets Rs 550-600 crore this year. Company appointed separate CEO just for this segment, treating it as independent operation. 

This work earns 25-30% margins versus 19% company average. As it grows, blended profitability rises without needing price hikes.

They can now machine turbine blisks and single-crystal metal parts, skills very few companies globally have. Blisks are rotating discs with blades attached, used inside jet engines. 

Making them requires cutting titanium or nickel alloys to extreme precision. Single-crystal parts are harder because metal has no grain boundaries, so conventional cutting fails. 

These capabilities move Sansera from making seat brackets and cargo parts to engine-level aerospace components where margins and barriers run far higher. 

New hangar and facility under construction, targeting Rs 8000-9000 crore revenue by decade end.
